dedupe_keys.name: hospit win experimental platform for a digital twin of patient pathways in a hospital

description: HospiT-Win is a proof-of-concept platform for building a digital twin of how patients move through a hospital, in which a simulated hospital stands in for the real one so that the twin can be developed and tested safely. The producers are Abdallah Karakra, Franck Fontanili, Elyes Lamine and Jacques Lamothe, named as authors in the release. It has two parts: an emulator, built in the WITNESS simulation software, that plays the role of the real hospital and generates patient pathway events, and the digital twin itself, built in FlexSim, which mirrors those events and can run what-if scenarios. Coverage is one generic hospital setting. The model files are available free on GitHub and Zenodo under an open licence, but both WITNESS and FlexSim are commercial products needed to run them. Caveats: an experimental prototype from 2021 with little documentation in the release, not connected to real hospital information systems. Simulation uses: prototyping hospital digital twins that track patient flows and test responses to surges, and teaching the emulator approach to twin development. Related records: the Gloucestershire hospital digital twin case (case_study-gloucestershire-hospital-digital-twin) describes a twin in use, and the SimPy healthcare models (model-simpy-streamlit-healthcare-des) offer open-source simulation of hospital queues.
